The people do whatever the priests do. I will punish them all for the bad things that they do. I will give them what their sins deserve.
They will eat, but they will still be hungry. They will have sex with prostitutes, but they will still have no children. This will happen because they have turned away from the Lord.
Instead, they worship other gods.

They ask wooden idols to tell them what to do! A stick tells them what will happen in the future! They have turned away from me and they have lost their way. They have not been faithful to me, their God, as a prostitute is not faithful to her husband.

They offer sacrifices on the tops of the mountains. They burn offerings on the hills. They do this under the oak trees, the poplar trees and the other big trees. They enjoy the shade under those trees. As a result, your daughters serve the false gods as prostitutes. Your sons' wives are also guilty of adultery.
But I will not punish them for those sins, because the men are just as guilty! They sleep with prostitutes. They join with prostitutes to offer sacrifices to the false gods.

You people of Israel are not faithful to the Lord. But do not let the people of Judah become guilty of the same sins. Do not travel to Gilgal to worship! Do not go to Beth Aven! Do not say, ‘I promise this is true, as surely as the Lord lives.’

Israel's people have turned against the Lord. They are like a young cow that refuses to obey its owner. So how can the Lord take care of them? Will he put them in a big field to eat the grass like lambs?
The people of Israel enjoy their idols. Do not go near them!
After they have drunk enough wine, they are happy to sleep with prostitutes. They enjoy doing things that should make them ashamed.
Now a strong wind will pick them up and take them away. They will become ashamed because of their sacrifices to false gods.

‘Listen to this, you priests! Listen carefully, you Israelites! Listen, you people of the royal family! You are guilty and you deserve punishment. You have caused trouble for people with your trap at Mizpah. You have caught people in your net at Tabor.
People have turned against me and they have murdered many people. So I will warn them all and I will punish them.
I know what the people of Ephraim are like. The Israelites cannot hide their sins from me. You are no better than prostitutes! You can no longer serve me as my people.
Yes, the sins of the Israelites do not allow them to return to me, the Lord their God. They are not faithful to me and they love to worship idols. They do not want to know me.

The Israelites are proud of what they do, and that shows that they are guilty. Their sins cause them to fall into great trouble. That will happen to the people of Israel and Ephraim. And the people of Judah will fall with them.
They take their sheep and cows to offer as sacrifices to the Lord. They want the Lord to help them, but he does not answer them. They cannot find him because he has gone away from them.
They have turned against the Lord. Their children do not belong to him. They enjoy the new moon feast. But that will soon destroy them and the crops in their fields.’
‘Make a noise with your horns in Gibeah!
The day for Ephraim's punishment will soon come.
The leaders of Judah are not honest.
Terrible trouble will come to Ephraim's people.
I will destroy the people of Ephraim,
Ephraim's people knew that they were ill.
I will attack Ephraim's people like a lion.
Then I will return to my place.
‘Listen! We should return to serve the Lord.
He will soon make us strong again.
We should respect the Lord's authority.
‘People of Ephraim and Judah,
I sent my prophets to warn you.
It is faithful love that makes me happy.
Like Adam, my people did not obey the covenant that I had made with them.
All the people of Gilead do evil things.
The priests join together like robbers.
I have seen people do disgusting things in Israel.
People of Judah, I will also punish you when the right time comes.
‘Yes, I want to make the people of Israel healthy again,
They do not understand that I remember all their sins.
The king is happy to see the evil things that his people do.
None of them serves me faithfully.
On a day when the king has a feast,
But the leaders are planning to murder the king.
The leaders are so angry that they kill their rulers.
‘Ephraim's people have mixed themselves with people of other nations.
Foreign people have taken away Israel's strength.
Israel's people are too proud to change.
Ephraim has become like a silly dove.
When they fly around like that,
Terrible trouble will happen to them,
They do not pray and trust me to help them.
I taught them what was right.
They do not look up to me for help.
The Lord says,
Israel's people call out to me for help.
But they have refused to do what is good and right.
My people chose kings to rule them,
People of Samaria, you have made an image of a calf as your idol.
That idol is not a true god!
Like a farmer, Israel's people have planted the wind.
Israel will become lost among the other nations.
Israel's rulers have gone to Assyria for help.
Yes, they have paid money to get friends who will help them.
Ephraim's people have built many altars to make sin offerings.
I carefully explained my laws to my people.
Israel's people offer sacrifices to me,
Israel's people have built beautiful palaces.
People of Israel, do not shout with joy,
But the threshing floors will not provide enough grain to feed the people.
The Israelites will not remain in the Lord's land.
They will not pour out wine as an offering to the Lord.
So what will you do on your festival days?
Listen! Perhaps some Israelites will escape when Assyria's army attacks.
The time for Israel's punishment has arrived!
God has sent his prophet to warn the people of Ephraim.
The Israelites do very wicked things,
The Lord says,
The great things that Israel enjoys will soon disappear.
But even if they do have children,
At one time, I saw that Ephraim's land was a beautiful place, like Tyre.
Lord, what should I ask you to give these people?
The Lord says,
Ephraim's people are very sick.
My God will not accept them as his people,
Israel was like a healthy vine that had lots of grapes.
They do not truly trust God.
Soon these people will say,
They promise to do many things,
The people who live in Samaria will be afraid.
Assyria's army will carry the idol away.
The people of Samaria and their king will come to an end.
The wicked altars on the hills will break into pieces.
The Lord says,
When I decide that the time is right,
Ephraim was like a cow that I had taught to stamp on grain.
Be like a farmer who plants good seed.
But instead, you have planted evil things.
So you will soon hear the noise of war.
The same thing will happen to you, people of Bethel,
The Lord says,
But the more I spoke to Israel's people,
I was the one who taught this child, Ephraim, to walk!
I loved them and I was kind to them.
But they refuse to turn back to me.
War will come to their cities.
My people have decided to turn away from me.
Israel, I cannot leave you alone.
I am very angry with you,
I will roar loudly like a lion,
They will return to me, like birds that fly from Egypt.
The Lord says,
Ephraim's people chase after useless things all the time.
The Lord is ready to accuse Judah's people in a court of law.
Before Jacob was born, he cheated his brother.
He fought against an angel and he won.
This was the Lord God Almighty!
So now, you must return to your God.
Your traders love to cheat people.
Ephraim's people proudly say,
God says,
I gave my messages to the prophets.
The people in Gilead do wicked things.
Jacob ran away to the land of Aram.
The Lord used a prophet to bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
But Ephraim's people have made the Lord very angry.
In past times, when the leaders of Israel spoke,
Now the Israelites continue to do more and more sins.
So those people will soon disappear!
The Lord says,
I took care of you in the wilderness,
I gave food to my people,
So I will attack them like a lion.
I will attack them like an angry bear that has lost her children.
I will destroy you, Israel.
What has happened to your king?
I was angry, but I agreed to give you a king.
I have a record of Ephraim's sin.
They will be in pain like a woman who is giving birth.
Will I save these people from the power of death?
Among the other nations, Israel has been successful.
Samaria's people are guilty
Israel's people, return to the Lord your God!
Return to the Lord and pray to him! Say to him,
Assyria cannot save us.
The Lord says,
I will bless Israel's people,
They will grow like a tree that makes new branches.
I will give my people shade to live in safely.
People of Ephraim, do not let me see your idols any more!
If you are wise, you should understand these things.
This is the Lord's message that he gave to Joel, son of Pethuel.
You leaders of Israel, listen to this!
Tell your children about it.
Great armies of locusts have eaten all our crops.
Wake up and weep, you people who have drunk too much wine!
A great army has attacked our land.
They have destroyed our vines.
Cry loudly, like a young woman who is wearing sackcloth.
There is no grain or wine that we can bring
The fields have no crops in them.
You farmers should be very upset.
The vines and the fig trees have no water
You priests, dress yourselves in funeral clothes!
Tell people that they must fast.
That will be a terrible day!
We stand and we watch
The seeds have died in the dry ground.
The cows move around as they look for grass to eat.
Lord, I call to you for help.
Even the wild animals are so thirsty
Make a loud noise with a trumpet in Zion!
It will be completely dark on that day.
As they move, they destroy everything in front of them.
They look like horses.
They make a noise like chariots
Nations are very afraid when they see this army.
The great army runs forward to attack.
They do not push against each other.
They quickly attack a city
The earth shakes as they move forward.
The Lord's voice shouts like thunder
The Lord says, ‘Even now it is not too late!
Show me that you are really upset.
No one knows what the Lord your God will do.
Make a loud noise with a trumpet in Zion!
Bring all the people together.
The priests should weep,
Then the Lord showed that he loved his land.
He answered them,
I will take the army from the north far away from you.
Land, do not be afraid!
Wild animals, do not be afraid!
Shout with joy, people of Zion!
Now there is plenty of grain on your threshing floors.
The Lord says,
You will have plenty to eat.
You will know that I am among my people in Israel.
After all that, I will pour out my Spirit on all people.
At that time, I will pour out my Spirit on all my servants,
I will cause strange things to appear in the sky
The sun will become dark.
At that time, everyone who calls to the Lord for help will be safe.
‘Listen! At that time, I will cause the people of Judah and Jerusalem to return.
Then I will bring all the nations together.
They threw dice to win my people for themselves.

What are you trying to do, you people of Tyre, Sidon and the regions of Philistia? Do you want to pay me back for something that I have done to you? If so, I myself will quickly pay you back with punishment.
You took my silver and my gold. You took all my valuable things to put in your own temples.
You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greek people. You sent them far away from their own country.
But now I will cause my people to return home. I will bring them back from the places to which you sold them. Then I will do to you what you have done to them.
I will sell your sons and daughters to the people of Judah. And they will sell them to the Sabeans, who live far away.
Tell this news to the people of all nations:
Take your ploughs
Come quickly, you nations that are all around.
‘All the nations must prepare themselves.
Bring your knives to cut down the crops!
Great crowds of people are in the Valley of Punishment.
The sun and the moon become dark.
The Lord shouts from Zion.
The Lord says,
On that day, the vines on the mountains
But Egypt will be an empty place.
Now Judah will for ever be a place where people can live safely.
But I will surely punish those who killed my people.

Amos was one of the shepherds who lived in the town of Tekoa. God showed Amos the things that would happen to the people of Israel. God did that two years before the earthquake came. It was during the time that Uzziah was the king of Judah. Joash's son, Jeroboam, was the king of Israel. This is the message that Amos received from God.

Amos said, ‘The Lord speaks loudly from Zion. Yes, he shouts from Jerusalem. As a result, the green fields will become dry and the grass will die. There will be nothing for the sheep to eat. Even the grass on Mount Carmel will die.’
The Lord says, ‘The people of Damascus have done more and more wrong things. So I will certainly punish them!
I will send a fire to destroy the palace that King Hazael built. It will destroy the strong buildings of King Ben-Hadad.

I will also break the strong gates of the city of Damascus. I will remove all the people who live in the Aven Valley. I will remove the king of Beth-Eden. Their enemies will take the people of Syria far away to Kir as prisoners.’ That is what the Lord says.
The Lord says, ‘The people of Gaza have done more and more wrong things. So I will certainly punish them.
So I will send a fire to burn the walls of Gaza. It will destroy the strong buildings in Gaza.

I will remove the king of Ashdod city. And I will remove the king who rules in Ashkelon city. I will punish the people who live in Ekron city. All the Philistines who remain will die.’ That is what the Lord God says.
The Lord says, ‘The people of Tyre have done more and more wrong things. So I will certainly punish them.
So I will start a fire on the walls of Tyre. And the fire will burn all the strong buildings. It will destroy them completely.’
The Lord says, ‘The people of Edom have done more and more wrong things. So I will certainly punish them.
So I will start a fire. And the fire will destroy the big city of Teman. The fire will also burn the strong buildings of Bozrah city.’
The Lord says, ‘The people of Ammon have done more and more wrong things. So I will certainly punish them.

So I will send fire. And the fire will destroy the walls of Rabbah. It will destroy the strong buildings too. People will fight and they will shout. They will shout loudly, like the noise that a strong wind makes in a storm.
The enemies will take away their king and their leaders. They will take them to another country. The king and the leaders will not be free to return.’ That is what the Lord says.
The Lord says, ‘The people of Moab have done more and more wrong things. So I will certainly punish them.

So I will send fire to the country called Moab. The fire will destroy the strong buildings in Kerioth town. The people will hear their enemies shout. And they will hear the sounds that their enemies' trumpets make. And the people will die.
I will let the enemies kill the ruler of Moab. And I will let them kill all its leaders too.’ That is what the Lord says.
The Lord says, ‘The people of Judah have done more and more wrong things. So I will certainly punish them.
So I will send fire to Judah. The fire will completely burn the strong buildings that are in Jerusalem.’
The Lord says, ‘The people of Israel have done more and more wrong things. So I will certainly punish them.
They are not kind to poor people and they do not help them. A father and his son have sex with the same woman. They do not respect the holy way that I want them to live.

When they lend money to poor people, they take the poor people's clothes as a guarantee. They do not return the clothes each night, as they should do. Instead they sleep on the clothes themselves. They do that at the places where they worship their gods. The rich people take money from poor people. They use that money to buy wine for themselves. Then they drink the wine in the temples of their gods.
Remember the Amorites. They were big and strong. They were like the tallest cedar trees and the strongest oak trees. But I destroyed all of them.
I brought you out of Egypt. After that, I led you through the wilderness for 40 years. Then I took you to the land where the Amorites lived, so that it would belong to you.
I chose some men among you to be prophets, and some to be Nazirites. You Israelites know that it is true.’ That is what the Lord says.
‘But you told the Nazirites to drink wine, like everyone else. And you said to the prophets, “Do not speak messages from God.”
So I will punish you. A cart that has a heavy load pushes down on the ground. That is how I will push down on you.

You might try to run away. But nobody will get free. Even the fastest runner will not get free. The strong people will not be strong enough to stop me. The soldiers will not be able to save their lives.
Soldiers who shoot arrows will have to turn back. Fast runners will not save their lives. Soldiers who ride on horses will also die.
At that time, strong, brave soldiers will run away without their clothes.’ That is what the Lord says.
You Israelites, listen to this message that the Lord speaks against you. This message is to all you people that he saved from Egypt.
He says, ‘There are many nations of people on the earth. But I chose you alone to belong to me. So I will punish you when you do wrong things.’
If two people travel together, they have first agreed to meet together.
If a lion roars in the forest, it means that he has killed an animal to eat. A young lion does not shout unless he has caught something.
If there is no food in a trap, a bird will not fly into it. If the door of the trap closes, it means that it has caught something.
Also, if the people in a city hear a trumpet's sound, they become very afraid. If bad trouble comes to a city, it means that the Lord has sent it.
Before the Lord God decides to send trouble, he first tells his prophets about it.
So now the lion has roared! Everyone should be afraid! The Lord God has spoken, so his prophets must tell his message.

Tell this message now in Ashdod city. Go to the strong cities in Egypt and speak the message there. Say this: ‘Come to the mountains in Samaria. Look at the cruel things that people are doing in Samaria. Many people are afraid.’
The Lord says, ‘People have forgotten how to be honest. They rob people and they store valuable things in their big houses. They become rich because they are so cruel.’
So the Lord God says, ‘Enemies will come to attack your land. They will destroy your strong buildings. They will take all your good things from you.’

The Lord says, ‘When a lion catches a young sheep, the shepherd will try to save as much as he can. He might save only two legs, or a small part of an ear. It will be the same for the Israelites who live in Samaria. They will escape with only a piece of a bed, or a bit of cloth.’
The Lord God Almighty said to me, ‘Listen! Go and warn the Israelites that they have done wrong things.
I will punish them because they have not obeyed my Law. I will destroy the altars at Bethel. The horns of the altar will break off and they will fall to the ground.

I will destroy all their houses, the homes that they live in during the winter, and the ones that they live in during the summer. I will completely destroy all their big, beautiful houses, with their valuable things made from ivory.’ That is what the Lord says.

Listen to this message, you women who live on the hill in Samaria. You are like fat cows that do not work hard for food. You are like the cows in Bashan. They eat on very good land by the Jordan River. You do not give to weak people what they need. You are not fair to poor people. Then you sit down and you say to your husbands, ‘Bring us more to drink.’
The Lord God has made this promise and he speaks only true words. He says, ‘The time will come, when your enemies will take you away with meat hooks and fish hooks.
There are places in your city's walls where people have broken the walls. Your enemies will pull you through those places and they will throw you out towards Harmon. None of you will stay here.’

The Lord also says, ‘You like to go to Bethel. You say that it is your holy place. And when you go there, you do wrong things. So go there, if you must, and do your bad things. Go to Gilgal, if you must, and do more bad things there. You bring your sacrifices there every morning as a gift. But that does not make me happy. Every three days, you bring your gifts. But that also does not make me happy.

You bring bread to say “thank you”. You even bring lots of it and you tell everyone, “Look at how much I have brought.” You really like to do that. So continue to do it, but it does not make me happy.’ The Lord God says this!
‘Earlier I made you hungry in all your cities. There was no food anywhere. But you did not start to pray to me again.’ The Lord says this!

‘Three months before your food was ready to pick, I did not send rain. So all the food became too dry. Sometimes I sent rain to one city, but I did not send it to other cities. I sent rain to one person's land, but I did not send it to another person's land. So that other person's land became too dry.
People became weak. They went from city to city to look for water. They were almost too weak to walk. There was not enough water. But still you did not start to pray to me again.’ The Lord says this!

‘I sent hot winds from the east. They burned the small plants, so those plants died. Worms made the other plants sick. So the other plants died. Locusts ate your trees that give fruit. But still you did not start to pray to me again.’ The Lord says this!

‘I caused many people among you to become very sick. It was like what happened many years ago in Egypt. At that time, very many people got sick. Then I sent soldiers to you. And they killed your young men and they took away your horses. The smell from dead bodies was very bad. But you still did not start to pray to me again.’ The Lord says this!

‘I killed many people among you, as I destroyed the cities called Sodom and Gomorrah. Some of you did not die. You were like a stick that is already burning. And someone saves it from the fire. But still you did not start to pray to me again.’ The Lord says this!
‘So I will send trouble to you Israelites again. Get ready! You will see it. Then you will know that I have come to judge you.
I made the mountains and I made the wind. I tell people what I have decided to do. I change dawn into night. I walk on the high places of the earth. My name is the Lord God Almighty.’
You people of Israel's family, listen to the sad song that I will sing about you:
‘You are like a young woman who died young, without children. Now you have fallen down and you will not rise up again. You lie there on the ground. There is nobody there to help you to get up.’

This is what the Lord God says to you: ‘1,000 soldiers will go out from a city to fight, but only 100 soldiers will come back. From another city, 100 soldiers will go out to fight, but only 10 will come back.’
To the people of Israel's family, the Lord says, ‘Come back to me and you will live.
Do not go to Bethel, Gilgal, or Beersheba. Do not try to find me there, because I am not there. I will send enemies to destroy those places. They will take the people away as slaves.’

Return to the Lord and you will live. If you do not do that, he will come like fire to punish you. He will completely destroy Joseph's descendants. Bethel and all its people will burn. Nobody will be able to stop the fire.
You people change what is right and true to make lies. You are not fair or honest.

The Lord made the groups of stars called Pleiades and Orion. The Lord changes the night into dawn, and he changes the day back to night again. He takes the water in the sea, and he pours it out as rain on the earth. The Lord is his name!
He quickly destroys strong people. He knocks down their strong buildings and their walls.
‘You Israelites hate honest judges. You laugh at anyone who speaks the truth.

You cheat poor people so that they pay too much tax. You take away their food for yourselves. Because of that, you will not live in the beautiful houses that you have built for yourselves. You will not drink wine from the vines that you have planted.

I, the Lord, know all the wrong things that you have done. They are very many and they are very bad. You are cruel to good people. You take bribes to tell lies. Sometimes a person gives money to you to make you tell lies. As a result, poor people do not receive justice.
This is such an evil time that clever people say nothing. That is how they keep themselves safe.’
You say that the Lord God Almighty is with you. Stop doing evil things. Do good things, so that you will live. Then the Lord God Almighty will really be with you, as you say.
Hate evil things and love good things. When you judge people, be fair and honest. Then maybe the Lord God Almighty will be kind to those of his people who still remain, Joseph's descendants.

The Lord, the Lord God Almighty says, ‘All the people will be sad. They will weep and cry loudly in all the streets. They will tell the farmers to weep with them. They will tell the singers to sing sad songs for them.
In every field and garden, people will be weeping, because I will come to punish them all.’ That is what the Lord says.
You want the great day of the Lord to come. But it will be very bad for you! You think that God will punish your enemies on that day. But that day will not bring light to you, it will bring darkness.
Nobody will escape! It will be like a man who runs away from a lion, but then he meets a bear! When he goes into his house to be safe, he puts his hand on a wall and a snake bites him!
Know this: The day of the Lord will be dark, not light. It will bring trouble, not joy.
The Lord says, ‘When you have your festivals, I hate them! When you meet to worship me, it does not make me happy!
When you bring burnt offerings and grain offerings to me, they do not please me. I will not accept your friendship offerings of fat animals.
When you sing songs to worship me, I will not listen. They are just noise! I do not want to hear the music of your harps.
What I do want to see is justice! I want to see that you always do what is right. Those good things should never stop, like a river that always runs with water.
You people of Israel's family, listen to me! I led you through the wilderness for 40 years. During that time, did you worship me with sacrifices and offerings? No!
Instead, you have idols that you have made for yourselves. You have the idol of Sakkuth, your king. You have the idol of Kaiwan, your star god. Now you will have to carry them with you.
I will send you away as prisoners. Your enemies will take you beyond Damascus.’

Trouble is coming to you people who live in Zion and on Samaria's hill. You think that you are safe. You think that you are important people who live in the best nation on earth. Israelite people respect you as their leaders.
Go and look at Calneh city. Go and look at Hamath city. Then go and look at Gath city, where the Philistines live. Are your cities stronger than their cities? Do you have more land than they do?
You refuse to think that trouble might come to you. But the cruel things that you do are causing trouble to come very soon.
You lie on beautiful, expensive beds. You do not work, but you rest all the time. You eat fat young sheep and cows.
Like King David, you play music on your harps and you sing new songs.
You drink lots of wine. You put beautiful oils on your bodies. But you are not sad that Joseph's descendants are destroying themselves as a nation.
You will be the first people that your enemies will take away as prisoners. You will no longer enjoy your feasts and wild parties.

The Lord God Almighty has promised that this will surely happen. He has spoken this strong message: ‘The Israelites think that they are very strong. But I have turned against them. I hate their strong buildings. So I will give their great city of Samaria and everything in it to their enemies.’
At that time, if ten people are safe together in one house, they will all die.
When a man comes to carry a dead body outside to burn it, he will ask his relative, ‘Is there anyone with you in the house?’
When the Lord gives his command, enemies will destroy all the houses, great and small. They will break them all into pieces.
Horses cannot run on rocks. People do not try to plough the sea. But you Israelites have changed what is fair and honest into something bad. You have made justice seem like poison.
You are proud because you won against Lo-Debar and Karnaim. You think that your own strength did that.

But the Lord God Almighty says to you Israelites, ‘I am sending an enemy nation to attack you. They will bring trouble to you everywhere, all the way from Lebo-Hamath in the north, to the Arabah Valley in the south.’

The Lord God showed a vision to me. I saw a crowd of locusts. The Lord was ready to send them to destroy the crops in the fields. They would come after we had taken the early crops to give to the king. Then the later crops were beginning to make grain.
I saw that the locusts came and they ate everything. I asked the Lord, ‘Lord God, please forgive your people. We cannot continue to live if those locusts destroy our food. We are too weak!’
Then the Lord decided not to do it. He said to me, ‘That will not happen.’
After that, the Lord God showed to me a vision of a fire. He was ready to send it to punish us. I saw that it caused the deep sea to become dry. It also burnt all the land.
I said, ‘Lord God, please do not do that! Your people cannot continue to live. We are too weak!’
Then the Lord decided not to do it. He said to me, ‘That too will not happen.’

Then the Lord showed this vision to me. The Lord God was standing next to a wall. In his hand was a string with a heavy weight on its end. The Lord was hanging the string down the wall. He was looking to see whether the wall was straight.
He asked me, ‘Amos, what do you see?’
I will send enemies to destroy the holy places of Isaac's descendants. All Israel's holy places will fall down. Enemies will use swords to kill King Jeroboam and his family.’

Amaziah was a priest at the holy place called Bethel. He sent a message to Jeroboam, the king of Israel. He said, ‘Amos is speaking against you among all Israel's people. What he is saying will deceive the people of our nation.
Amos is saying, “Our enemies will kill King Jeroboam. They will take all the people to a foreign country as prisoners.” ’
Then Amaziah said to Amos, ‘Go away, you prophet! Go back to your own country, Judah. Speak your messages from God to get your food there!
Do not speak God's message here in Bethel any longer. It is where our king and our nation come to worship.’
Then Amos answered Amaziah, ‘My job was not as a prophet. My father never did that work. My job was to work as a shepherd. I also took care of fig trees.
But the Lord told me to leave my work as a shepherd. He told me to go and to speak his message to his people, the Israelites.
So listen to the Lord's message to you! You are telling me, “Do not speak God's message against Israel. Do not say that trouble is coming to Isaac's descendants.”

The Lord says this to you, Amaziah: “Your wife will work as a prostitute in the streets. Your sons and daughters will die in war. Enemies will measure your land into separate pieces and they will give it to others. They will take your people away from here as prisoners to a foreign country. And that is where they will die.” ’
Then the Lord God showed another vision to me. I saw a basket with summer fruit in it.
He asked me, ‘Amos, what do you see?’
On the day that I come to punish them, people will not sing in the temple. Instead they will weep loudly. There will be dead bodies everywhere. Be quiet now!’ That is what the Lord God says.
So listen to me, you who are cruel to helpless people. You try to destroy people who are poor and weak.

You say to yourselves, ‘We want the new moon festival to finish so that we can sell food again. We want our Sabbath day of rest to finish so that we can sell grain.’ But when you sell things, you cheat the people who buy from you. You deceive them with false weights, and you make the price too high.
When poor people cannot pay their debts, you buy them as your slaves. You pay a silver coin to buy them, which would not even buy a pair of shoes. You also mix dust with the grain that you sell.
The Lord has promised this: ‘You proud descendants of Jacob, I will never forget the wrong things that you have done.

The whole country will shake because of your sins. Everyone who lives there will weep. The ground will rise up, like the floods of the River Nile in Egypt. Then it will go down again, like the water of the Nile.’
The Lord God says, ‘At that time, I will make the sun go down at noon. I will make the earth become dark in the daytime.

Your parties will become funerals. You will not sing happy songs but you will weep. You will wear rough clothes and you will cut off all your hair. You will be as sad as if your only son had died. That will be a very bad day for you.’
The Lord God says, ‘Listen to me! At that time, I will cause you to be very hungry. It will not be because you need food and water. Instead, everyone in the land will want to hear a message from me.
People will travel everywhere in the country, north and south, east and west. They will want to hear a message from the Lord, but there will be nothing for them to hear.
At that time, your beautiful young women and your young men will become very thirsty. They will be weak and tired.

They worship Samaria's idols. They use the names of those false gods to make promises. They say, “In the name of the god of Dan,” or “In the name of the god of Beersheba.” Those people will fall down and they will never get up again.’

Then I saw a vision of the Lord. He was standing beside the altar in the temple. The Lord said, ‘Hit the tops of the pillars so that the whole foundation shakes! Cause the building to fall on the heads of all the people. If anyone is still alive after that, I will cause them to die in battle. Nobody will escape!
They might try to dig deep into the earth to save themselves. But my strong hand will pull them out of there. They might climb up into the sky. But I will pull them down from there.

They might try to hide on the top of Mount Carmel. But I will find them and I will take them from there. They might try to hide from me deep down in the sea. But I will command the great sea snake to bite them.
Even when their enemies take them away as prisoners, I will cause them to die in battle. I have decided to destroy them. I will not help them.’

The Lord God Almighty will do this! When he touches the earth, it shakes. Everyone who lives there weeps. The ground rises up, like the water of the River Nile in Egypt. Then it goes down again, like the river.
The Lord builds his palace up into heaven, with its foundation on the earth. He takes up the water from the sea, and he pours it out on the earth as rain. The Lord is his name.

The Lord says, ‘You Israelite people, do not think that you are more important to me than the people of Ethiopia. It is true that I led you safely out of Egypt. But I also brought the Philistines from Crete. And I brought the Aramean people from Kir.

I, the Lord God, am carefully watching you Israelites. I see that you are a wicked nation, so I will remove you from the earth. But I will not completely destroy all the descendants of Jacob.’ That is what the Lord says.
‘Listen to me! I will cause trouble to come to Israel's family, as they live among other nations. It will be like a person who shakes a sieve to remove dirt from grain.
Those among my people who do bad things will die. They say, “God will not send trouble to us. Nothing bad will happen to us.” But their enemies will kill those bad people in war.’

The Lord says, ‘When that time comes, I will make David's kingdom strong again. It has become like a broken hut, but I will repair it. I will cause it to become as good and strong as it was when King David ruled.
You Israelites will fight the Edomites who still remain. You will win against them and the other nations that once belonged to me.’

The Lord says, ‘The time will come when food will grow very well in your fields. People will need to work quickly to cut down all their crops before they plough the ground to plant again. Lots of grapes will grow on your vines. People will work quickly to make wine from the grapes before they plant new vines. So much juice will pour out of the grapes that it will run down the hills!

I will bring the people of Israel, my people, back to their own land. Enemies destroyed their cities, but now my people will build them again. They will live safely in them. My people will plant vines. They will drink wine from their grapes. They will eat the fruit from trees that they have planted in their gardens.
And I will plant my people in their own land. That is the land that I have given to them, and nobody will ever pull them out of that land.’
This is the vision that Obadiah saw.
The Lord says to Edom,
You are proud that you are very strong.
You might try to fly high in the sky like an eagle.
‘If robbers came to rob you in the night,
Esau's people will lose everything!
Even the nations who have been your friends
The Lord says,
Brave soldiers from Teman will be very afraid.
You were cruel to Jacob's descendants.
A foreign army attacked Jerusalem and they went into the city.
When your brothers were in great trouble,
When my people were in great trouble,
You waited beside the road from the city.
The day of the Lord will come soon.
You went on my holy hill and you drank there.
But on Mount Zion, there will be people who are free again.
Jacob's descendants will be like a hot fire.
Israel's people from the Negev Desert
The strong group of Israel's people who have been in exile will return.
The people who have become free
The Lord spoke a message to Jonah, Amittai's son.
He said, ‘Go now to the great city of Nineveh. Tell the people in the city that I know how wicked they are. Tell them that I will punish them because of their sins.’

But Jonah did not want to obey the Lord's command. He decided to run away to Tarshish. He went down to Joppa. There he found a ship that was ready to sail to Tarshish. After he had paid for the journey, he got into the ship. He wanted to go on the ship to Tarshish, to get far away from the Lord.
Then the Lord sent a strong wind on the sea. The storm was so powerful that it almost broke the ship into pieces.

The sailors were very frightened. Each of them called out to his own god for help. They threw into the sea all the things that the ship carried. They wanted to make the ship as light as they could. Jonah had gone down into the bottom of the ship. He was lying down and he was asleep.
The ship's captain went to Jonah. He said, ‘Why are you sleeping like that? Get up now! Call to your god for help! Maybe he will listen to us and we will not die.’
Then the sailors said to each other, ‘We should throw dice to find out who has brought all this trouble to us.’ So they threw dice. The dice showed that Jonah had caused the storm.
So they said to Jonah, ‘Tell us, who has caused all this trouble for us? What is your job? Where do you come from? What country do you live in? Who is your family?’
Jonah answered them, ‘I am a Hebrew man. I worship the Lord who is the God of heaven. He made the sea and the land.’
This made the sailors even more afraid. Jonah had already told them that he was running away from the Lord. So they said to him, ‘Why did you do a thing like that?’
The waves in the sea were becoming bigger because of the storm. So the sailors asked Jonah, ‘What should we do to you so that the sea becomes quiet?’
Jonah replied, ‘Pick me up and throw me into the sea. Then the sea will become quiet. It is because of me that you are in danger from this great storm.’
But the sailors did not do what Jonah said. Instead, they tried to use oars to drive the ship back to the land. But the storm was too strong and they could not do that.

So the sailors called aloud to the Lord. They prayed, ‘Lord, please do not punish us with death if we have to kill this man! Do not say that we are guilty because we have killed someone who has done nothing wrong. Lord, we know that you have sent this storm because you wanted to do it.’
Then the sailors took hold of Jonah and they threw him into the sea. The storm stopped and the sea became quiet.
When they saw what had happened, the sailors became very afraid of the Lord's power. They offered a sacrifice to him and they promised that they would serve him.
But the Lord sent a great fish to swallow Jonah. Jonah was inside the fish's stomach for three days and three nights.
From inside the fish's stomach, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God.
He said,
You threw me into the deep water,
I said to myself,
The deep water of the sea covered me,
I went very deep in the water,
When my life was nearly gone, I prayed to you, Lord.
Idols cannot help.
But as for me, I will sing to thank you.
Then the Lord told the great fish to spit Jonah out from its stomach. So it dropped Jonah onto the shore.
The Lord spoke to Jonah a second time.
He said, ‘Now go to that great city, Nineveh. Tell the people there the message that I will give to you.’
Jonah obeyed the Lord and he went to Nineveh.
When Jonah arrived in Nineveh, he walked for one day into the city. Then he shouted out to the people, ‘After 40 more days, God will destroy Nineveh.’

The people who lived in Nineveh believed God's message. They told everyone that they must not eat any food for several days. Everyone had to wear sackcloth to show that they were sorry. The most important people and the ordinary people all did that.
The king of Nineveh heard about God's message. He got up from his throne and he removed his royal clothes. He dressed himself in sackcloth and he sat in ashes on the ground.
Then the king sent this message to all the people in Nineveh. He said, ‘This command comes from the king and his officers. No person or any of your animals may eat any food or drink any water.
Everyone must wear sackcloth. You must cover all your animals with sackcloth too. Everyone must pray to God with all their strength. You must all stop doing bad and cruel things.
Then perhaps God may agree to forgive us. He may decide that he will not be angry with us. Then perhaps we will not all die.’
God saw what the people in Nineveh did. He saw that they stopped doing evil things. He had said that he would punish them for their sins. But now he decided that he would not destroy them.
Jonah was not happy when God decided not to destroy Nineveh. He became very angry.

He prayed to the Lord. He said, ‘Lord, this is what I thought would happen when I was still at home. So I decided to run away to Tarshish, so that you could not be kind to the people of Nineveh. I know that you are a God who is very kind. I know that you forgive people. You do not become angry quickly. You always show your faithful love for people. Even when you have said that you will punish people, you decide that you will not do it.
Lord, please kill me now! I would rather die than continue to live.’
The Lord replied to Jonah, ‘You are not right to be so angry.’
Jonah went out of Nineveh. He built a little hut on the east side of the city. He sat in the shade of the hut. He waited to see what would happen to the city.
The Lord God made a little plant grow there. He caused it to grow up over Jonah's head. It gave him shade from the hot sun. This comforted Jonah in his trouble. Jonah was very happy about the plant.
But at dawn the next day, God sent a worm to attack the plant. So then the plant died.
When the sun rose, God caused a hot wind to blow from the east. The hot sun shone on Jonah's head so that he became very weak. He wanted to die. He said, ‘I would rather die than continue to live.’
But God said to Jonah, ‘You are not right to be so angry about the plant.’

But the Lord said to Jonah, ‘You are upset about what happened to this little plant. But you did not plant it. You did not help it to grow. It grew up quickly during one night and then it died the next night. You are sorry about such a little thing!

So it is right for me to be sorry about Nineveh. It is a great city. More than 120,000 people live in it. They cannot understand the difference between what is right and what is wrong. They also have many farm animals.’

This is the message that the Lord gave to Micah, who was born in Moresheth. Micah told this message to the people when Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah ruled Judah as kings. God showed Micah what would happen to the cities of Samaria and Jerusalem.
Hear this, all you people of the world!
Look! The Lord is leaving his home!
The mountains will melt under his feet,
All these things will happen
So the Lord says:
I will break all Samaria's idols into pieces.
Because of this trouble, I will cry aloud and I will weep.
Samaria has bad wounds that will not get better.
Do not let our enemies in Gath know about our trouble!
You people who live in Shaphir,
The people of Maroth hope for something good to happen.
You people of Lachish,
You will have to say ‘goodbye’ to the people of Moresheth Gath.
People of Mareshah, the Lord will send an army to attack you.
People of Judah, show that you are very sad.
Terrible trouble will happen to people who do wicked things.
They take from other people the fields that they want for themselves.
So the Lord says this:
At that time, your enemies will laugh at you.
A time will come when the Lord's people receive their land again.
The people answered me,
You descendants of Jacob should not talk like that!
The Lord says:
You take for yourselves the beautiful homes of my people's women.
Get up and go away!
A prophet might come to you
Descendants of Jacob, I will bring you all together again.
The one who has power to open a way will lead them out.
Then I said,
But you hate what is good,
You are like butchers who think that my people are meat.
One day, the wicked people will call to the Lord for help,
The Lord says, ‘I say this about the false prophets who are deceiving my people:
Because of that, it will become like night for you prophets.
Then the prophets and diviners will all be ashamed.
But as for me, the Lord's Spirit fills me with power.
So listen to this, you leaders of Jacob's people.
You use murder and violence
Jerusalem's leaders accept bribes
Because of how you live, this is what will happen.
In the last days, the mountain of the Lord's temple will be great.
As they come, people from many nations will say,
The Lord will judge between the people of many nations.
Everyone will sit under their own vine and under their own fig tree.
People of other nations serve their own gods.
The Lord says,
They are like weak people who cannot walk properly.
And as for you, Jerusalem,
Jerusalem, it seems that you are shouting loudly
Yes, you people of Zion should shake and scream,
Many nations have now come together to attack your city.
But they do not know the Lord's thoughts.
The Lord says,
People of Jerusalem, prepare your soldiers to fight!
‘I speak to you, Bethlehem Ephrathah.
So the Lord will put Israel's people under the power of their enemies.
This ruler will take his place as king.
He is the one who will give peace to his people.
These leaders will use their weapons
Jacob's descendants who remain
Jacob's descendants who remain
Israel's people, you will win against your enemies.
The Lord says,
I will destroy the cities in your land.
I will remove the magic things that you use.
I will remove the idols and the stone pillars
I will pull out the Asherah poles that you worship.
I will also punish the people of all nations that refuse to obey me.
Listen to what the Lord says:
Mountains and strong foundations of the earth,
My people, what bad things have I done to you?
I brought you out of Egypt.
My people, remember how King Balak of Moab wanted to hurt you.
When I come to meet the Lord,
Perhaps he will accept a gift of a thousand male sheep,
No! The Lord has told each of you what is good.
Listen to the Lord as he calls to the city of Jerusalem!
I will not forget the wicked things that you do.
I will not forgive you when you use false scales.
The rich people among you use violence
So I will punish you with pain because of your sins.
You will eat, but you will not have enough.
You will plant seeds for crops,
You have obeyed the evil laws of King Omri
I am very sad and upset!
No faithful people now remain in the land.
They have learned how to do wicked things with both hands!
Even the best person is as useless as a thorn bush.
Do not trust anyone, even your special friend.
At that time, sons will not respect their fathers.
But as for me, I will continue to hope in the Lord.
My enemies, do not be happy because I am in trouble.
I have not obeyed the Lord,
When my enemies see this,
The time will come when you will build again the city's walls.
At that time, people of other nations will come to you.
But the earth will become an empty desert,
Lord, we belong to you as your people.
The Lord says,
People of other nations will see the Lord help his people.
They will move low along the ground,
Lord, there is no God like you.
You will be kind and forgive us once again.
You will be faithful and you will continue to love us,
This is a message that God showed as a vision to Nahum, who lived in Elkosh. It is a message about the people of Nineveh.
The Lord wants people to worship only him.
The Lord does not quickly become angry,
When he shouts a command at the sea, it becomes dry!
He causes the mountains and the hills to shake.
When the Lord is angry, nobody can stop him.
The Lord is good!
But he will quickly destroy Nineveh.
Any plan that you make to hurt the Lord will be useless.
He will completely destroy his enemies.
Someone who makes wicked plans has come out from you, Nineveh.
This is what the Lord says:
Now I will make you free from Assyria's power.
The Lord has spoken this command about you, king of Assyria. He says,
People of Judah, look towards the mountains!
An enemy is coming to attack you, people of Nineveh.
Now the Lord will make Jacob's descendants great again.
Strong soldiers are coming to attack you, Nineveh!
They drive their chariots very fast through the streets.
The army leader commands his best soldiers to go forward.
They open the river gates and water pours into the city.
Nineveh's people must leave their city with much shame.
Nineveh is like a pool of water.
The enemy's soldiers say to each other,
The enemy takes every valuable thing from the city.
What has happened to the great city of Nineveh?
Nineveh's men were like lions
But now the Lord Almighty says to Nineveh's people,
Terrible things will happen to you, Nineveh.
Listen to the sound of the enemy as they attack Nineveh!
The chariot drivers make their horses run forward to the battle.
This has happened because Nineveh has lived like a beautiful prostitute.
The Lord Almighty says to Nineveh,
I will throw dirty rubbish at you.
When anyone sees you,
Your city is no better than Thebes.
Thebes trusted in the great power of Ethiopia and Egypt.
But Thebes' enemies took her people away as prisoners.
Now you people of Nineveh will also become like men who are drunk.
All your strong buildings are like fig trees
Look at your soldiers!
Enemy soldiers will be all around the city, so get ready!
But fire will destroy your city.
You have many traders in your city.
Your guards and your officers are also like a crowd of locusts.
King of Assyria, your leaders are now asleep.
Your life will come to an end,
This is the message that God showed to his prophet Habakkuk.
Lord, how long must I call out to you for help?
You cause me to see many things that are not right.
The law has no power to make things right.
‘All of you, look carefully at the other nations.
I will give more power to the Babylonians.
They cause people to be very afraid.
Their horses run faster than leopards.
Their whole army comes to do violent things.
They insult kings,
Their army quickly moves on to another place,
Lord, you have always been God,
But you are too holy to accept anything that is evil.
It seems that you have made people like fish in the sea.
The Babylonians can easily catch them,
Their nets give them everything that they need,
Will you let them continue to do that?
I will stand at my place on the wall of the city. I will watch from there. I will wait to see what God will say to me. I have complained to him and now I will see how he answers me.
The Lord answered me. He said:

What I will show you must happen at the time that I have decided. That is a future time, but it will certainly happen, as I have said. It may not happen very soon, but you must be patient. What I show you will certainly happen at the right time, so wait for it.
Look now! The enemy is very proud. They do not want to do what is right. But righteous people will live because they are faithful to God.

Wine will destroy that proud enemy. They do not stop attacking other people. They never have enough for themselves. They are like death that is so hungry that it eats as much as it can. The deep hole of death eats everything. The cruel enemy is like that! They want all the nations to belong to them. They catch everyone to be their prisoners.

But one day, their prisoners will laugh at them. The people will insult that proud nation with songs and proverbs. They will say, “You have stored for yourselves many valuable things that do not belong to you. It will be very bad for you! You have robbed other nations so that you can be rich. This will not continue much longer!”
The people that have lent their riches to you will suddenly attack. They will come to take back their things and you will be very afraid. Now they will come to rob you!
You have robbed many nations. You have murdered people in many lands. You have destroyed towns and the people who live in them. Now the people who remain will come to rob you.

It will be very bad for anyone who cheats other people so that he can make his family rich. He thinks that his riches will make him safe. He thinks that he is too high up for any trouble to reach him.
But the cruel things that you have done will bring shame to your family. You decided to destroy people from many countries. Because of that, you will pay with your own life.
The stones in the walls of your houses will cry out against you. The beams in your roof will also shout aloud.
It will be very bad for anyone who kills people so that he can build a city for himself. It will be bad for anyone who does wicked things to make his town great.
Listen! The Lord Almighty has commanded this: All the work that people do to get things for themselves is useless. The things that the nations work so hard to get will become smoke!
But people everywhere will one day recognize the Lord's great glory. Those people will fill the whole earth, as the waters fill the sea.

It will be very bad for you! You cause your neighbours to become drunk. You are so angry that you make them drink too much wine. You are happy when they are so drunk that you can see their bare bodies.

But it is you who will become ashamed, not great. You will become drunk so that people see you with no clothes on! The Lord has a cup of wine in his right hand. He is ready to give it to you as a punishment. You will no longer be great, but you will be ashamed.

You have done cruel things to the people in Lebanon. You destroyed their animals. The Lord will punish you for the things that you have done, and you will be very afraid. You have murdered people. You have destroyed the land and the towns and the people who live in them.

What value does an idol have? What help can it give? Somebody has made it as the image of a false god. It can only tell false messages. Why should its maker trust it for help? He has used wood or metal to make it and it cannot speak!

It will be very bad for anyone who says to a piece of wood, “Wake up!” It will be bad for anyone who says to a stone that cannot speak, “Get up and help me!” It cannot teach you! It has gold or silver to make it look nice, but it is not alive.
But the Lord rules from his holy temple. Everybody on the earth should be quiet in front of him.’
These are the words that the prophet Habakkuk prayed. He used special music to sing it.
Lord, I have heard the report about you.
God is coming from Teman!
He is as bright as the sunrise.
As he marches to war,
God stands ready to fight,
I see the tents where Cushan's people live,
Was it the rivers that made you angry, Lord?
You have prepared your bow.
The mountains see you and they shake.
You shoot your bright arrows
You angrily march across the earth.
You have marched out to rescue your people,
You threw his own spear into his head,
But you, Lord, marched across the sea with your horses.
I listened to this
Whatever happens, I will continue to thank the Lord.
I will still sing to thank the Lord!
The Lord God causes me to be strong.

This is the Lord's message, which he gave to Cushi's son, Zephaniah. Cushi was the son of Gedaliah. Gedaliah was the son of Amariah, and Amariah was the son of Hezekiah. The Lord gave this message to Zephaniah when Josiah ruled Judah as king. Josiah was the son of Amon, king of Judah.
The Lord says,
I will destroy people and animals.
‘I will attack Judah
I will destroy the people who worship the sun, the moon and the stars.
I will destroy those people who have turned away from me, the Lord.
Be quiet and listen to the Lord God!
The Lord says,
At that time, I will also punish everyone
The Lord says,
Weep, you people who live near Jerusalem's market!
At that time, I will use lamps to find people in Jerusalem
But their enemies will take away their valuable things.
The great day of the Lord will soon be here.
It will be a day when God shows his great anger.
There will be the loud noise of trumpets.
The Lord says,
On that day when the Lord shows his anger,
Come together! Yes, come together now!
The Lord has decided the day for your punishment,
Turn to the Lord,
No people will remain in Gaza.
Terrible trouble will come to you people who came from Crete,
Your land beside the sea will become fields
The land will belong to the people of Judah's tribe who are still alive.
The Lord says,
The Lord Almighty, Israel's God, says,
God will punish the people of Moab and Ammon as they deserve.
The Lord will cause them to be very afraid.
The Lord will also punish you people of Ethiopia.
The Lord will attack the people who live in the north.
Sheep, goats and cows will lie down there,
All this will happen to that proud city,
Terrible trouble will come to this city!
The people of the city do not obey any laws.
The city's rulers roar like lions
The city's prophets are proud people
But the Lord is in the city
The Lord says,
I thought, “Now you people of Jerusalem will respect me!
So you must wait for me to act.
‘At that time, I will change people
My people who now live far away, beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,
At that time, you people of Jerusalem will not be ashamed,
But I will leave a group of poor and humble people among you.
The Israelites who remain will be honest people.
Be happy and sing, you people of Zion!
The Lord has taken away the punishment that you deserved.
On that day, people will say to Jerusalem,
The Lord, your God, is with you.
The Lord says,
Listen to me! At that time, I will punish
At that time, I will bring you back together
The Lord told his prophet Haggai to say this to the people:
‘You people are living in beautiful houses. But my temple is still just a heap of stones! It is time for you to do something about it!
I, the Almighty Lord, tell you this: Think carefully about what is happening to you.

You plant seeds but not many plants grow to give you food. You never have enough to eat. You drink, but you are still thirsty. You have clothes to wear, but they do not keep you warm. When you receive money for your work, you soon need to spend it. Then you have no money left.
The Almighty Lord also says this: Think about how you live your lives.
Now go up to the hills to get wood to build my temple again. If you do that, I will be happy. You will worship me there as you should do.

You thought that you would get a lot of food from the crops that grow in your fields. But only a few plants grew. When you brought your food home, it quickly disappeared. I blew it away! Why do you think all this happened? It happened because my temple is still a heap of stones. At the same time, you all work hard to build your own houses. I, the Almighty Lord, am telling you this!
That is why there has been no rain on your fields. That is why your plants do not grow well.

I have stopped the rain, so that your fields and the hills have become dry. Your crops will not grow. There will be no grapes to make wine. You will not have olives to make oil. Nothing will grow in the ground. Your animals will not become fat. People and animals will all suffer. For all your work, you will get nothing.’

Zerubbabel and Joshua, the leader of the priests, as well as all the people obeyed the Lord, their God. They were the people that the Lord had brought back to Jerusalem from Babylon. When they heard the message that Haggai spoke to them, they agreed that it was a message from the Lord. As a result, they respected the Lord and they decided to obey him.
Haggai, the Lord's prophet, then spoke this message from the Lord: ‘The Lord says, “I am with you.” ’
In that way, the Lord gave strength to Zerubbabel, Joshua and all the people who had returned to live in Jerusalem. They decided to work hard to build the temple of their God, the Almighty Lord.
They started to work on the 24th day of that same month, in the second year after Darius had become king.
On the 21st day of the seventh month, the Lord spoke again to Haggai, his prophet.

The Lord told Haggai that he must speak to Zerubbabel and to Joshua. Shealtiel's son, Zerubbabel, was the ruler of Judah. Jehozadak's son, Joshua was the leader of the priests. The Lord also told Haggai to speak his message to all the people who had returned to live in Jerusalem. The Lord told Haggai to say this to them all:
The Lord says, ‘Some of you will remember how beautiful my temple was in past times. Look at it now! It seems nothing like it was before.

But now, Zerubbabel, be strong and brave! Joshua too, and all you people who belong here in Judah, be strong and brave! Now begin to work, because I am with you to help you. That is what I, the Almighty Lord, say to you.
Do not be afraid. Remember that I made a promise to your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt. I promised them that I would be with them. My Spirit is now with you too.
I, the Almighty Lord also tell you this: Soon, I will cause the heavens and the whole earth to shake. I will also cause the sea and the land to shake.

I will cause people in all the nations of the world to shake with fear. They will come here to offer their valuable gifts. At that time, I will cause my temple to be full of glory. I, the Almighty Lord, tell you this.
Yes, all the silver and gold in the world belongs to me. And I promise you this:
This new temple will be even more beautiful than the old temple in past times. Here in this place I will bless my people.’ That is what the Almighty Lord says.
The Lord spoke again to Haggai, his prophet, on the 24th day of the ninth month, in the second year since Darius had become king. This was the Lord's message:
The Almighty Lord says, ‘Ask the priests a question about my Law.

A person might be carrying some special, holy meat in his clothes. His clothes might then touch some food. It might be bread, or soup, or wine, or oil. If the clothes that hold the holy meat touch any other food, does that other food also become holy?’
Haggai asked the priests another question: ‘If anyone touches a dead body, you know that you become unclean. If an unclean person touches any of these foods, would they also become unclean?’

So Haggai told them, ‘This is what the Lord says: This nation and its people are like that. They are unclean. So everything that they do is also unclean. All the gifts that they offer to me are unclean. I could not accept them.
Think carefully what life was like before you started again to build the Lord's temple. Do not forget that.
In those days, you hoped to get 20 bags of grain from your fields. But you only got ten bags. You hoped to get 50 jars of wine from your grapes. But you only got 20 jars.
I sent bad weather and other problems to destroy all your crops. All your hard work came to nothing. But you still did not return to worship me, your Lord.
Remember today, the 24th day of the ninth month. You have started again to build my temple. Now you have built its foundation, think about what will happen from today.
You have already eaten the crops that you stored. The grapes, figs, pomegranates and olives are not yet ready for you to pick. But after today, I will bless you. You will have many good things.’
On the same day, the Lord spoke to Haggai again. He said,
‘Speak to Zerubbabel, the ruler of Judah. Tell him that I will cause the sky and the whole earth to shake.

Tell him that I will destroy the power of foreign kings. I will destroy their armies. Their horses and chariots will fall down. Their soldiers will fight against each other. They will kill each other with their swords.

But I, the Almighty Lord say this to you, Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel. You are my servant and I have chosen you. On that special day, I will give to you the authority to rule on my behalf. That is the message of the Almighty Lord.’

The Lord gave his message to the prophet Zechariah in the second year that Darius ruled Persia as king. It happened in the eighth month of that year. Zechariah was the son of Berekiah and the grandson of Iddo.
This was the Lord's message:
So you must say to the people, ‘The Lord Almighty says, “You must turn back to me, and I will return to you.” That is the message from the Lord Almighty.
He says, “Do not be like your ancestors. Many years ago the prophets told them, ‘Stop doing those evil and wicked things.’ But they refused to obey me.
Your ancestors have been dead for a long time. Those prophets also are no longer alive.

But my commands and my laws which the prophets spoke to the people are still true. I punished your ancestors, as I had warned them. Then they turned back to me. They said, ‘The Lord Almighty has punished us as we deserved for our sins. He has done as he said he would do.’ ” That is what the Lord says.’

On the 24th day of Shebat, the 11th month of the year, the Lord gave his message to the prophet Zechariah, the son of Berekiah and the grandson of Iddo. This happened in the second year that Darius ruled as king.
During the night I had a vision. I saw a man who was sitting on a red horse. The horse was standing among some myrtle trees in a valley. Behind him there were red, brown and white horses.
I asked the angel who was talking with me, ‘Please sir, what is the meaning of these horses?’
Then the man who was standing among the myrtle trees said, ‘The Lord has sent these horses to go and look in all the places on the earth.’

The men on the other horses agreed with the angel of the Lord who was standing among the myrtle trees. They said, ‘We have gone to look at things all over the earth. We have seen that everywhere is now resting in peace.’

Then the angel of the Lord said, ‘Lord Almighty, how long will you be angry with Jerusalem before you are kind to them? How long will you be angry with the cities of Judah? You have already been angry with them for 70 years.’
The Lord answered the angel who was speaking to me. He spoke kind words to the angel.
The angel then spoke to me again. He said, ‘Give this message to the people. Tell them clearly that the Lord Almighty says, “I love Jerusalem and Mount Zion very much. It is my special place.
I am very angry with the nations which think that they are safe. I was a little bit angry with my own people, but those nations caused my people to suffer too much.”

So this is what the Lord says: “Now I will return to Jerusalem and I will be kind to the people there. I will build my house there again.” That is what the Lord Almighty says. “Builders will measure the land in the city and they will build houses there again.”

Tell the people clearly that the Lord Almighty says, “The towns where my people live will have great riches again. I will cause the people of Zion to live in peace. I will show that I have chosen Jerusalem as my own special city.” ’
Then I looked up and I saw four horns.
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, ‘What are these horns?’
Then the Lord showed me four workers with hammers.
I said, ‘What are these men coming to do?’
Then I looked up and I saw a young man in front of me. He had a string in his hand that he could use to measure things.
I asked the man, ‘Where are you going?’
The angel who had been speaking with me now went away from me. Another angel came to meet him.

The second angel said to the first angel, ‘Run to that young man. Tell him, “Jerusalem will no longer be a city that has walls around it. This is because there will be many people and many animals that live in it.
The Lord himself promises that he will protect Jerusalem. He will be like a wall of fire around the city. His own glory will shine inside the city.” ’
This is the Lord's message: ‘Run away! Escape from the country in the north where you have been prisoners. I sent you away in every direction, north, south, east and west.
Now escape, you people of Zion! Return home from Babylon where you have been living.’

Return home, because the Lord Almighty has sent me, Zechariah, with a message. He has sent me to warn the nations who have robbed you. He will use me to bring glory to himself. You are his special people. If anyone hurts you, it is the same as if they hurt God's own eye.
The Lord says, ‘I will use my power to punish your enemies. Even their own slaves will rob them.’ When that happens, you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
The Lord says, ‘Sing and be happy, you people of Zion. Yes, I am coming to you! I will live among you.

At that time, people will come from many nations to worship me, the Lord. They will become my people too. And I will make my home among you all.’ When that happens, you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
Judah will again belong to the Lord as his special place in his own land. He will choose Jerusalem as his own city.
So be quiet now, people everywhere, as you stand in front of the Lord. He is ready to move from his holy home in heaven to do great things.

In another vision I saw Joshua, the leader of the priests. He was standing in front of the angel of the Lord. Satan stood at the right side of Joshua. He was ready to say that Joshua had done bad things.

The Lord said to Satan, ‘The Lord says that you are wrong, Satan. The Lord has chosen Jerusalem for himself. He says that you are wrong! Joshua is like a stick that someone pulls quickly out of the fire to keep it safe.’
Joshua was wearing very dirty clothes when he stood there, in front of the angel.
The angel said to the people who stood around him, ‘Remove his dirty clothes.’ Then he said to Joshua, ‘See what I have done. I have taken away your sin. Now I will give you new clothes to wear.’
Then I said, ‘Put a clean hat on his head.’ So they put a clean hat on his head and they dressed him in new clothes. The angel of the Lord stood near to them while they did this.
Then the angel of the Lord spoke seriously to Joshua.

He said, ‘The Lord Almighty says to you, “You must live in ways that please me. You must do the things that I tell you to do. If you do that, you will rule over my temple and all its yards. I will allow you to come with the angels who are standing around you.

Joshua, leader of the priests, you and all the other priests who are sitting with you must listen carefully. You are all like a sign of what will happen in the future. Yes, I will bring my servant, who is called the Branch.

Look! I have put a big stone in front of Joshua! It has seven sides. I will cut the words of a message in the stone. The message is that I will remove the sin of this guilty land in one day.” That is what the Lord Almighty says.
He says, “On that day, you will all ask your friends to come and sit with you. They will sit safely with you under your own vines and fig trees.” ’
Then the angel who had been speaking with me returned. He woke me up, like someone who had been asleep.
He asked me, ‘What do you see?’
I also see two olive trees that are standing beside the lampstand. One tree is on the right side of the bowl and one tree is on the left side.’
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, ‘What do these lamps mean, sir?’
He said, ‘Do you not know what these lamps are?’

Then the angel said to me, ‘These lamps are a picture of the message that the Lord says to Zerubbabel: “Your own strength and your own power will not give you success. It is my Spirit that will give you success.” That is what the Lord Almighty says.

It may seem that a great mountain stands in front of Zerubbabel. But it will become flat ground! One day, Zerubbabel will bring the last stone to finish the temple building. Then the people will shout, “God is kind! He will bless it!” ’
Then the Lord's message came to me again. He said,
‘Zerubbabel has built the foundation of the temple. He will also finish the building.’ When that happens, you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.

It may seem that only a little work has begun. But do not think that it is useless. The seven eyes of the Lord see everything that happens in the world. They will see Zerubbabel as he continues the work on the temple building. That will cause everyone to be happy.
Then I asked the angel, ‘What are these two olive trees that stand on the right side and on the left side of the lampstand?’
I also asked him, ‘I see two branches of the olive trees that are pouring olive oil through the two gold pipes. What is the meaning of those branches?’
The angel replied, ‘Do you not know what they are?’
So the angel said, ‘They are the two leaders that the Lord of the whole earth has chosen to serve him.’
I looked up again. I saw a scroll that was flying in the air.
The angel asked me, ‘What do you see?’

The angel said to me, ‘The words on the scroll are a curse that is going out over the whole land. The curse tells about punishment for people who rob other people. God will remove them from the land. God will also remove from the land those people who tell lies against other people.

The Lord Almighty says, “I will send out this scroll to take a curse into the house of robbers. I will also send it into the house of people who use my name to tell lies. The curse will remain in their houses. It will completely destroy all the wood and the stones of their houses.” ’
Then the angel who was speaking to me came forward. He said, ‘Look up. See the thing that has now appeared.’
I asked, ‘What is it?’
There was a heavy metal lid that covered the basket. As I looked, the angel lifted up the lid. I could see a woman who was sitting in the basket.
The angel said, ‘This woman shows what sin is.’ Then he pushed her down into the basket again. He put the heavy metal lid back on top of the basket.
Then I looked up and I saw two women. They had strong wings, like the wings of a large bird. The wind carried them towards me. They lifted the big basket up high into the sky.
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, ‘Where will these women take the basket?’

The angel said to me, ‘They will take it to the country of Babylon. They will build a temple for it there. When the temple is ready, they will put the basket in it. They will put it in a place of honour there.’
I looked up again and I saw four chariots. They came out from between two mountains that were made of bronze.
The first chariot had red horses to pull it. The second chariot had black horses.
The third chariot had white horses. The fourth chariot had grey horses. All the horses were strong.
Then I asked the angel who was speaking with me, ‘What are these chariots, sir?’
The angel answered me, ‘These are the four spirits of heaven. They have come from the Lord of all the earth.
The chariot with the black horses is going towards the north country. The chariot with the white horses is going after them. The chariot with the grey horses is going towards the south country.’

When these strong horses came out, they were in a hurry to leave. They wanted to travel everywhere on the earth. The Lord had told them, ‘Go and look everywhere in the whole earth.’ So that is what the horses did.
Then the Lord called to me. He said, ‘Look! The horses that have gone to the north country have caused my Spirit to have peace. I am no longer angry about the north country.’
The Lord gave this message to me:

‘Three men have come back from Babylon, where they were prisoners. Their names are Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah. Take the gifts that they have brought with them. Then go immediately to the house of Zephaniah's son, Josiah.
Use some of the gold and silver to make a royal crown. Then put it on the head of Jehozadak's son, Joshua, the leader of the priests.
Say to Joshua, “The Lord Almighty says, ‘Here is the man whose name is the Branch. He will grow and become great in this place. He will build the Lord's temple.

Yes, he is the one who will build the Lord's temple. He will wear royal clothes. He will sit on his throne and he will rule his people as their king. There will be a priest with him on his throne. They will both completely agree with each other as they work together.’ ”
They will put the crown in the Lord's temple. It will cause people to give honour to Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah and Zephaniah's son Josiah.

People will come to Jerusalem from places that are far away. They will help to build the Lord's temple. When this happens, you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you. It will happen if you remember to obey the commands of the Lord your God.’
In the fourth year that Darius was king, the Lord spoke to Zechariah. It happened on the fourth day of the ninth month that is called Kislev.
At that time, the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-Melech and their men to Jerusalem. They came to ask the Lord to bless them.

They came to the temple of the Lord Almighty to speak to the priests and to the prophets. They asked, ‘Should we continue to weep and to fast in the fifth month each year? We have done this for many years.’
The Lord Almighty then gave this message to me.

He said, ‘Speak to all the people in this land and to the priests. Tell them, “You were prisoners in another country for 70 years. At that time, you were sad and you fasted in the fifth month and in the seventh month of each year. But you did not really do this to give me honour.
Also, when you eat and you drink at special times, you do that to please yourselves.” ’

This is the same message from the Lord that the prophets spoke in past years. At that time, many people lived in Jerusalem and they were happy. Many people also lived in the towns around Jerusalem, in the Negev region and in the low hills in the west.
The Lord spoke again to Zechariah.
He said, ‘This is what the Lord Almighty says to the people: “Be sure that you do what is right and fair. Be kind and help each other.
